mission1.title: Beg. Borrow. Steel.
mission1.success_message: You've completed Mission 1: Beg. Borrow. Steel. You defined your 'why,' made a real commitment, mapped your hidden resources, built your support squad, and faced rejection head-on. You're no longer in the 'thinking' phase—you're in the 'doing' phase. The foundation is laid. You are ready for Mission 2.

badge_config.title: Resourceful Founder
badge_config.description: Completed Mission 1: Beg. Borrow. Steel. Mastered asking, faced rejection, and mapped your initial founder assets.

quests.title: The New Beginning

badge_config.title: Pathfinder
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 1: Defined your core why, made a real commitment, and faced your initial fears.

notes.title: Honesty is your compass
notes.content: Resist the urge to edit yourself. These answers are for you, not a potential investor. The strongest businesses are built on personal truth.

notes.title: This might feel uncomfortable
notes.content: That's the point. Comfort is where dreams go to die. You're here to build something real.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 1: The New Beginning. You know your 'why,' you've made a commitment, and you've faced your fears. That's more than most people ever do. On to the next quest.

tasks.title: Why Start?
tasks.briefing_text: Let's be totally honest. Building a business takes serious energy, and vague goals fade the moment life gets busy. What is the actual change you want to make in your life?

resources.title: Why Your 'Why' Matters More Than Your Idea

tasks.reflection_prompt: Look at your 'why_statement.' Does it resonate with you on a gut level? If not, tweak it now. This will be your anchor.

challenges.title: The 5-Minute Timer
challenges.description: Set a timer for 5 minutes. Write non-stop about why you're starting. Don't edit. Don't judge. Just write.

tasks.title: Make It Real
tasks.briefing_text: Big goals require clear constraints. Let's set realistic expectations for your time, money, and launch timeline. Be honest, not aspirational.
tasks.reflection_prompt: Look at your weekly hours. Is this a realistic, sustainable commitment for the next few months? If you can only do 2 hours a day, own that and build your plan around it.

tasks.title: What's Scaring You?
tasks.briefing_text: Acknowledging your fears is a sign of strength, not weakness. Let's get them out in the open. This helps the program tailor its support for you.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the scariest roadblock on this list? We can help you with that. Let's make a plan.

quests.title: What You've Got

badge_config.title: Asset Mapper
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 2: Mapped your connections and audited your skills to unlock hidden leverage.

notes.title: Your network is your net worth
notes.content: Your friends, family, former colleagues, and online networks are powerful assets. Let's map them.

notes.title: Be generous with yourself
notes.content: Most people underestimate their skills. If you've done it, even once, it's a skill. List it.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 2: What You've Got. You've mapped your network and skills. You're not starting from zero—you have assets. Now let's put them to work.

tasks.title: Map Your Network
tasks.briefing_text: Who do you know? Your friends, family, former colleagues, and online networks are powerful assets. Let's map your 'social footprint' so you can see how to reach your first customers.

resources.title: How to Network Without Being Creepy
Launch yourself before your business - Guide to building your presence
Your Network is Your First Sales Channel

tasks.reflection_prompt: Who is the most valuable person in your network right now? Why? Consider reaching out to them casually this week.

challenges.title: The Connection Challenge
challenges.description: Find 5 people in your network you haven't talked to in over a year. Send them a message. Ask how they're doing.

tasks.title: Skill Inventory
tasks.briefing_text: Business is mostly about problem-solving. What are you good at? List your skills and expertise.
tasks.reflection_prompt: List your top 3 to 5 skills. How could these skills help a potential customer solve their problem?

quests.title: Start Asking

badge_config.title: Fearless Asker
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 3: Assembled your support squad, introduced yourself online, and made real asks.

notes.title: Start safe, then stretch
notes.content: We're going to start with people who already care about you—your squad. Then we'll stretch to people who don't know you yet.

notes.title: This will feel uncomfortable
notes.content: That's the point. Asking is a skill, and like any skill, it gets easier with practice. The worst they can say is no.

notes.title: You're offering something
notes.content: Remember, you're not asking for a favor. You're offering a chance to be part of your journey. People love to help.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 3: Start Asking. You've built your squad, introduced yourself to the community, and asked for a discount. You're now officially an 'asker.' The fear of asking is fading. Next up: chasing rejection.

tasks.title: Build Your Squad
tasks.briefing_text:
Your success hinges on a support system. Send a short message to 3-5 people (friends, family, colleagues) and tell them you're starting a business and ask if they'd be part of your 'cheer squad' to follow your progress and hold you accountable. Use the template below—just customize it.

Template: Hey [Name], I'm starting a business and I need people in my corner. Would you be willing to be part of my 'cheer squad'? I'll share my weekly progress with you. All you need to do is check in and hold me accountable. No heavy lifting—just your support. Would you be up for that?

resources.title: How to Build Your Support System

tasks.reflection_prompt: Who did you ask? What was their reaction? Having a support network is your secret weapon.

tasks.title: Say Hello
tasks.briefing_text: The Urge community is your tribe. Your first step is to introduce yourself. Share your 'why_statement' and what you're hoping to build.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What is one thing you're most excited to learn from the community?

tasks.title: Ask for Something
tasks.briefing_text: Now you're warmed up. Let's make a bigger ask. Find a service, tool, or product you use (or want to use) for your business and ask for a discount or a better deal. This could be a software subscription, a freelance service, or even a coffee shop. Practice asking without hesitation.
tasks.reflection_prompt: How did it feel? What was the response? You've just proven you can ask for something. Now, think about how much easier this will feel next time.

challenges.title: The 3-Ask Challenge
challenges.description: Make 3 asks this week. At least 1 should be to someone you don't know well. Track what happens.

scenarios: Ask a local coffee shop barista for a 10% founder discount.
Ask a colleague or peer for a 15-minute quick feedback session on your idea.
Ask an Uber driver if you can play DJ and connect to their car audio to play your custom hype song.

quests.title: No Is Just Data

badge_config.title: Rejection Master
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 4: Collected 'Nos', made bold asks, and conquered the fear of rejection.

notes.title: Rejection is not reflection
notes.content: Rejection is not a reflection of your worth. It's data. A 'no' today is a 'not yet' or a 'not this way.'

notes.title: The real goal
notes.content: The goal isn't to get a 'yes.' The goal is to get comfortable with asking. The 'yes' will come later.

notes.title: This will feel uncomfortable
notes.content: That's the point. Growth lives just outside your comfort zone.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 4: No Is Just Data. You've faced rejection, made bold asks, and survived. You're now more resilient than 99% of people who never ask. You're ready for Mission 2.

tasks.title: Practice Getting Nos
tasks.briefing_text:
Your challenge: Get 2 'No's. This could be from asking people for feedback on an idea, asking for a sale, or any other reasonable request where 'No' is a possible response. The goal is to collect them. Each 'No' is a data point and a step forward.

Suggested scenarios:
• Ask a stranger for directions to a place you already know (see if they say no)
• Ask a friend to buy your product/service (even if it doesn't exist yet)
• Ask a local business if they'd partner with you (without a clear proposal)
• Ask someone for a big favor (like covering your shift or lending you money)
tasks.reflection_prompt: What did you learn from each 'No'? Did any of them give you a reason why that could be helpful?

scenarios: Ask a coffee shop barista if you can step behind the counter and steam your own milk / pour your own espresso shot.
Ask a flight attendant or gate agent if you can get a free upgrade to First Class on your flight.
Ask a stranger on the street if they would be willing to learn a dramatic 10-second secret handshake with you.
Ask a bookshop or retail staff member if you can make a quick announcement on their store loudspeaker.

tasks.title: The Bold Ask
tasks.briefing_text:
Now it's time for the real test. Make a request that you're 95% sure will get a 'no.' Ask for something big, bold, or unreasonable. The goal isn't to get a 'yes'—it's to prove to yourself that rejection won't kill you.

🔥 Examples of bold asks:
• Ask a celebrity or influencer for a call
• Ask a company for free lifetime access to their product
• Ask a local business to give you something for free
• Ask someone to introduce you to their most valuable contact
• Ask for a 90% discount on something

💡 The more unreasonable, the better. You're not trying to get a yes. You're trying to get comfortable with rejection.

resources.title: The Art of the Bold Ask

tasks.reflection_prompt: You just made a bold ask. You probably got a 'no.' And you're still standing. That's the whole point. You're now more resilient than 99% of people who never ask.

challenges.title: The Bold Ask
challenges.description: Make a request that you're 95% sure will get a 'no.' Ask for something big, bold, or unreasonable. Track what you learn.

scenarios: Ask a brand or company you love if you can become an official ambassador, tester, or campus rep.
Ask an event host or conference organizer if you can give a 5-minute lightning talk or join a panel.
Ask a local business, creator, or community if you can design custom merch, posters, or graphics for them.
Ask someone directly if they would be willing to pay you  to solve a specific problem or chore for them.
Ask a neighbor or classmate if you can join them for a home-cooked dinner or host a shared potluck meal.

tasks.title: Are You Ready to Get Started?
tasks.briefing_text: You've done the hard work—you asked, faced rejection, and proved to yourself that it's completely harmless. Now, reflect on your journey, measure your mindset shift across key confidence metrics, and lock in your key takeaways.

resources.title: Rejection Is the Price of Admission

tasks.reflection_prompt: You've proven something to yourself today. Looking at the growth goals you just set, what is the most important mindset shift you need to achieve them?

mission2.title: Discovery
mission2.success_message: You've completed Mission 2: Discovery. You've mined your own frustrations, observed the people around you, researched the wider world, and picked the best opportunity to pursue. You're no longer searching—you have a direction. Mission 3 awaits.

badge_config.title: Opportunity Architect
badge_config.description: Completed Mission 2: Discovery. Uncovered market pains, evaluated ideas objectively, and committed to a high-potential direction.

quests.title: Mine Yourself

badge_config.title: Self Miner
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 1: Mined your daily frustrations and skills to uncover high-leverage business opportunities.

notes.title: Start with yourself
notes.content: The best problems to solve are the ones you understand deeply. Your frustrations are a goldmine.

notes.title: Don't overthink
notes.content: List everything that annoys you—big or small. We'll filter later.

notes.title: This is not about solutions
notes.content: Don't try to solve anything yet. Just observe and document the problems.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 1: Mine Yourself. You've identified problems from your own life and skills. You're building a foundation for your business.

tasks.title: Spot Your Frustrations
tasks.briefing_text: Your own frustrations are the most accessible problems to solve. What annoys you? What wastes your time? What feels broken? List them all—big and small.

resources.title: How to Spot Frustrations in Your Daily Life

tasks.reflection_prompt: Look at your frustrations. Which one feels the most urgent? Which one do you wish someone would solve?

challenges.title: The Frustration Log
challenges.description: For one week, write down every frustration you encounter. Big or small. At work, at home, in public. Just observe.

tasks.title: Turn Frustrations Into Opportunities
tasks.briefing_text: Now let's reframe your frustrations as business opportunities. A frustration is just an unsolved problem. An unsolved problem is an opportunity.

resources.title: How to Turn Problems Into Opportunities
Why Frustrations Make the Best Businesses

tasks.reflection_prompt: Which of your frustrations could someone pay to have solved? Why?

tasks.title: Audit Your Skills
tasks.briefing_text: Your skills are assets. What are you good at? What do people ask you for help with? What comes naturally to you? These are potential business opportunities.

resources.title: How to Identify Your Most Valuable Skills

tasks.reflection_prompt: Which of your skills could help someone solve a problem? Who needs this skill?

tasks.title: Skills as a Business
tasks.briefing_text: Your skills can be a business. What's a problem you could solve using your skills? Who would pay for that?

resources.title: How to Turn Your Skills Into a Business
What Skills Are People Willing to Pay For

tasks.reflection_prompt: How could you package your skills as a service or product? What would be the simplest version?

quests.title: People Watching

badge_config.title: Keen Observer
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 2: Observed real-world complaints and identified target audience pain points.

notes.title: You are a detective
notes.content: Look at the people around you. What problems do they have? What do they complain about?

notes.title: Listen more than you talk
notes.content: The best insights come from listening—not to answers, but to frustrations.

notes.title: Don't start with solutions
notes.content: Just observe. Don't try to fix anything. You're gathering data.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 2: People Watching. You've observed problems in your immediate circle. These people are your first potential customers.

tasks.title: Be a Detective
tasks.briefing_text: Put on your detective hat. Look at the people around you—friends, family, colleagues, neighbors. What problems do they have? What frustrates them? What do they complain about?

resources.title: How to Observe Problems in Others
People Are the Best Problem Sources

tasks.reflection_prompt: Look at your observations. Which problem feels the most urgent? Which one do you think you could help solve?

challenges.title: The 5 Conversations Challenge
challenges.description: Have 5 conversations this week where you ask people about their biggest frustrations—and just listen.

tasks.title: Spot the Opportunity
tasks.briefing_text: Now turn your observations into opportunities. For each problem you observed, what could be a solution? Who would pay for it?
tasks.reflection_prompt: Which of these problems could be the foundation of a business? Why?

quests.title: The Wider World

badge_config.title: Market Explorer
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 3: Scanned online communities, macro trends, and marketplaces to spot hidden demand gaps.

notes.title: Think bigger
notes.content: Your immediate circle is just the beginning. The world is full of problems waiting to be solved.

notes.title: Explore new spaces
notes.content: Visit forums, read comments, check trends. Problems are everywhere.

notes.title: Don't get overwhelmed
notes.content: You're exploring. Not committing. Gather as many problems as you can—you'll filter later.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 3: The Wider World. You've discovered problems beyond your immediate circle. Your opportunity set is now diverse.

tasks.title: Search the Communities
tasks.briefing_text: Online communities are goldmines. Reddit, Facebook Groups, LinkedIn communities, Quora—people are actively discussing their problems. Go find them and turn a repeated complaint into a business opportunity seed.

resources.title: How to Find Problems in Online Communities

tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the most common problem you're seeing in these communities? Why do you think it's common?

challenges.title: The Deep Dive
challenges.description: Spend 2 hours diving deep into a community or industry you know nothing about. What problems do they discuss?

tasks.title: Ride the Trends
tasks.briefing_text: Trends are signals. What's changing? What's new? What's growing? These changes create new problems—and new opportunities. Capture a trend-driven opportunity seed.

resources.title: How to Spot Problems in Trends

tasks.reflection_prompt: What trend is creating new problems? Who is being affected by these changes?

tasks.title: The Marketplace Scanner
tasks.briefing_text: Marketplaces tell you what people are already paying for. They reveal gaps, complaints, and underserved needs. Go scan Etsy, Fiverr, Upwork, Amazon—what problems are being solved poorly? Seed the opportunity gap.

resources.title: How to Spot Opportunities in Marketplaces
Marketplace Love Notes and Breakup Letters

tasks.reflection_prompt: What's a problem that people are trying to solve but no one is solving well? Where's the gap?

quests.title: The Decision

badge_config.title: Decisive Founder
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 4: Scored opportunities objectively, picked your target problem, and passed the decision gate.

notes.title: This is the hard part
notes.content: You've gathered opportunities. Now you must choose. Don't fall in love—evaluate objectively.

notes.title: Perfect is the enemy of started
notes.content: No opportunity is perfect. Choose the one that's good enough to start.

notes.title: Trust your gut
notes.content: The data matters. But so does your instinct. Don't ignore it.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 4: The Decision. You've evaluated your opportunities, picked the best one, and committed to a direction. You're no longer searching—you're building. Mission 3 awaits.

tasks.title: Score Your Opportunities
tasks.briefing_text:
Now it's time to evaluate your opportunities. For each one, score it against 5 criteria. This isn't about finding the 'perfect' opportunity—it's about finding the one that's best for you, right now.

Scoring Criteria (1-5):
• Passion: How excited are you about this problem?
• Urgency: How badly do people need this solved?
• Workaround Spend: How much are people already spending to solve this?
• Unfair Advantage: Do you have a unique edge?
• MSP Feasibility: Can you build a Minimum Sellable Product quickly?
tasks.reflection_prompt: Look at your highest-scoring opportunity. Why did it score so high? What makes it the most promising?

tasks.title: Pick Your Opportunity
tasks.briefing_text: You've scored all your opportunities. Now it's time to pick one. Don't overthink—choose the one that feels right based on the scores and your gut.

resources.title: How to Commit to an Idea

tasks.reflection_prompt: Why did you pick this opportunity? What made it stand out from the others?

tasks.title: Make It Official
tasks.briefing_text: This is it. You're either committing to this opportunity or going back to discover more. There's no wrong choice—but there is a choice.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's your biggest hesitation about this opportunity? Address it now.

mission3.title: Getting Real
mission3.success_message: You've completed Mission 3: Getting Real. You've validated your problem with real customers, defined your Minimum Sellable Product, understood your environment, and made a conscious decision about your business. You're no longer dreaming—you're building with intention. Mission 4 awaits.

badge_config.title: Validated Strategist
badge_config.description: Completed Mission 3: Getting Real. Validated customer pain, defined your MSP, and made an intentional Go/No-Go decision.

quests.title: The Deep Dive

badge_config.title: Problem Master
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 1: Conducted real customer interviews and defined a crystal-clear customer persona.

notes.title: From opportunity to problem
notes.content: In Mission 2, you found an opportunity. Now we're turning it into a problem to solve. This shift in perspective is critical.

notes.title: Details matter
notes.content: The more specific you are about the problem, the easier it will be to build a solution that actually works.

notes.title: Be specific
notes.content: If your problem statement could apply to anyone, it applies to no one. Get specific.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 1: The Deep Dive. You now understand your problem intimately—when it happens, who it affects, and what people do about it.

tasks.title: Talk to Customers
tasks.briefing_text: This is the most important task in Mission 3. Talk to 5 real people who have this problem. Don't pitch your solution—just listen. Understand their pain.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What surprised you most in these interviews? What did you learn that you didn't expect?

tasks.title: Define the Problem
tasks.briefing_text: You found an opportunity. Now let's turn it into a clear problem statement. The better you understand the problem, the better your solution will be.

resources.title: How to Write a Problem Statement

tasks.reflection_prompt: Looking at your problem statement, would someone who has this problem recognize themselves in it? If not, go deeper.

challenges.title: The 5-Why Challenge
challenges.description: Ask 'why' 5 times to get to the root cause of your problem. Don't stop at surface-level answers.

tasks.title: Create Your Customer
tasks.briefing_text: Create one customer persona. Focus on one person who has this problem. The more specific, the better.
tasks.reflection_prompt: Would this person recognize themselves in this persona? If not, go back and add more detail.

quests.title: Build to Sell

badge_config.title: MSP Architect
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 2: Designed a lean, focused Minimum Sellable Product ready for market execution.

notes.title: Build to sell, not to validate
notes.content: Your goal isn't to build something that might work. It's to sell something that does work.

notes.title: Start small
notes.content: The smallest sellable thing is the fastest path to learning. You can always expand later.

notes.title: Resist scope creep
notes.content: Your first version should feel almost embarrassingly small. That's how you know it's right.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 2: Build to Sell. You've defined your Minimum Sellable Product. It's small, focused, and ready to sell.

tasks.title: How Will You Solve It?
tasks.briefing_text: There are many ways to solve a problem. Let's explore four approaches and pick the one that fits your customer best.
tasks.reflection_prompt: Why did you choose this approach? What makes it the best fit for your customer?

challenges.title: The 7-Day Build
challenges.description: Can you build your MSP in 7 days? If not, it's too big. Cut it down.

tasks.title: Define Your MSP
tasks.briefing_text: Describe your Minimum Sellable Product in one sentence. The smallest thing you can sell right now.

resources.title: What Is a Minimum Sellable Product?

tasks.reflection_prompt: Is this something you could sell today? If not, it's too big. Cut it down.

tasks.title: Build Your MSP
tasks.briefing_text: Now let's define everything about your MSP—price, delivery, resources, timeline, and differentiation.
tasks.reflection_prompt: Would you buy this? At this price? For this value? Be honest.

quests.title: Know the Battlefield

badge_config.title: Landscape Analyst
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 3: Mapped competitive workarounds and verified essential business compliance requirements.

notes.title: Know your battlefield
notes.content: Understanding the environment is as important as understanding the problem. What's working? What's hard? Where are your customers?

notes.title: Your real competition
notes.content: Your competition isn't other companies. It's the workaround—people doing it themselves.

notes.title: Be honest about risks
notes.content: The biggest risks are the ones you don't see coming. Name them.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 3: Know the Battlefield. You understand the landscape, the trends, and the compliance requirements. You're ready to make an informed decision.

tasks.title: Map the Landscape
tasks.briefing_text: Let's map the environment. What trends make this problem relevant? Who else solves it? What's working? What's hard? Where are your customers?
tasks.reflection_prompt: Looking at this landscape, what's your biggest opportunity? What's your biggest threat?

tasks.title: Check Your Compliance
tasks.briefing_text: Every business has compliance requirements. Based on your solution type and industry, we'll generate a checklist of what you need to check before you start.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the biggest compliance requirement you need to address before launching?

quests.title: Go or No-Go

badge_config.title: Decisive Gatekeeper
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 4: Assessed project viability, faced worst-case scenarios, and passed the official Go/No-Go gate.

notes.title: This is the hardest part
notes.content: Making a conscious decision—yes or no—is harder than building. But it's the most important.

notes.title: Be honest about the risks
notes.content: If you can't name your biggest risk, you haven't thought it through.

notes.title: Trust your gut
notes.content: The data matters. But so does your instinct. Don't ignore it.

quests.success_message: You've completed Mission 3: Getting Real. You've validated your problem, defined your MSP, understood the environment, and made a conscious decision. You're no longer dreaming—you're building with intention. Mission 4 awaits.

tasks.title: Check Your Viability
tasks.briefing_text: Let's do a final viability check. Answer these questions honestly. This isn't about being optimistic—it's about being real.

resources.title: How to Know If Your Idea Is Good

tasks.reflection_prompt: If this didn't work out, what would you regret more—starting or not starting?

tasks.title: Face the Worst Case
tasks.briefing_text: Let's face the worst-case scenario. What if this doesn't work? What if you build it and no one buys? The goal isn't to scare yourself—it's to prepare yourself.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the worst that could happen? And what would you do next?

tasks.title: Make the Call
tasks.briefing_text: This is it. Based on everything you've learned—the problem, the customer interviews, the MSP, the landscape, the viability check—make a conscious decision.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the one thing that pushed you to this decision?

mission4.title: The Business Engine
mission4.success_message: You've completed Mission 4: The Business Engine. You've defined your offer, set your price, built your acquisition plan, run the numbers, and made a conscious decision. You know exactly how your business makes money—or if it can at all. Mission 5 awaits.

badge_config.title: Engine Builder
badge_config.description: Completed Mission 4: The Business Engine. Modeled pricing, customer acquisition channels, and unit economics.

quests.title: Shape Your Offer

badge_config.title: Offer Architect
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 1: Defined your promise, focused feature sets, and mapped the customer experience.

notes.title: Your offer is your promise
notes.content: Your offer isn't just a list of features. It's a promise to solve a problem. Get the promise right, and the features follow.

notes.title: Start with the customer
notes.content: What does your customer actually want? Not what you want to build. What they want to buy.

notes.title: Resist the temptation to add more
notes.content: A clear offer beats a complicated one every time. The best offers are simple.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 1: Shape Your Offer. You have a clear value proposition, a focused feature set, and a mapped customer experience. You know what you're selling.

tasks.title: Your Promise
tasks.briefing_text: What's the core promise you're making to your customer? What's the one thing they get that they can't get elsewhere? Your value proposition is the heartbeat of your offer.

resources.title: How to Write a Value Proposition
The Value Proposition Is Not the Features

tasks.reflection_prompt: If your customer could only remember one thing about your offer, what should it be? That's your value proposition.

challenges.title: The 2-Minute Test
challenges.description: Can you explain your offer in 2 minutes to a stranger? Practice until they say 'I get it.'

tasks.title: What's In, What's Out
tasks.briefing_text: Brain dump all the features your solution could have. Don't filter, don't prioritize. Just list everything you can imagine. We'll filter in the next task.
tasks.reflection_prompt: Look at your list. What features are you most excited about? Which ones are you dreading? That's a signal.

tasks.title: Pick Your Focus
tasks.briefing_text: Now let's be ruthless. From your brainstorm, pick 3 must-have features for your first version. Then list what you explicitly won't include. This is where the magic happens.
tasks.reflection_prompt: You're saying 'no' to features. How does that feel? The best founders get comfortable with saying 'no' to good ideas so they can say 'yes' to great ones.

tasks.title: The Journey
tasks.briefing_text: Map the customer experience from payment to delivery. What happens after they give you money? Walk through each step.
tasks.reflection_prompt: Put yourself in your customer's shoes. What are they feeling at each step? Where does the anxiety or confusion happen?

quests.title: Price It Right

badge_config.title: Value Pricer
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 2: Named your price confidently based on value perception, not fear.

notes.title: Price is a statement
notes.content: Your price says something about your product. Too cheap and it feels low-quality. Too expensive and it feels out of reach.

notes.title: Value first, cost second
notes.content: The right price is what your customer would willingly pay for the value they receive. Not what you need to survive.

notes.title: Don't underprice
notes.content: First-time founders almost always underprice. You can always go down. Going up is much harder.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 2: Price It Right. You have a confident price based on value, not fear.

tasks.title: Name Your Number
tasks.briefing_text: Let's set your price. Start with what the problem costs your customer, then what they pay for alternatives, then name your number.
tasks.reflection_prompt: If you were your customer, would you pay this price? Why or why not?

challenges.title: The $1,000 Test
challenges.description: If your customer had $1,000 to spend on solving this problem, what would they spend it on? Are you in the top 3 choices?

tasks.title: Test Your Price
tasks.briefing_text: Now let's stress-test your price. Would customers pay double? Is it fair? Does it feel trustworthy?
tasks.reflection_prompt: If your price feels 'too cheap,' you might be sending the wrong signal. What would make it feel premium?

quests.title: Find Your Customers

badge_config.title: Acquisition Planner
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 3: Selected a focused acquisition channel, crafted compelling messaging, and built an acquisition plan.

notes.title: Focus is everything
notes.content: First-time founders die by trying five channels at once. Pick ONE channel and master it.

notes.title: Your first 10 customers
notes.content: If you can't name where you'll find your first 10 customers, you don't have a channel.

notes.title: Start small
notes.content: You don't need a website. You need one customer. Start there.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 3: Find Your Customers. You have a focused channel, a clear message, and a realistic acquisition plan.

tasks.title: Pick Your Channel
tasks.briefing_text: Where do your first 10 customers come from? Be specific. If you can't name the place, you don't have a channel.
tasks.reflection_prompt: Why did you pick this channel over all others? What makes it your best first bet?

challenges.title: The 1-Customer Challenge
challenges.description: Try to get just one customer this week. Not 10. Not 100. Just one.

tasks.title: Craft Your Message
tasks.briefing_text: What will you say? What's your exact offer or message? Why should they stop scrolling and buy today?
tasks.reflection_prompt: Would you respond to this message? If not, rewrite it until you would.

tasks.title: Assess Your Plan
tasks.briefing_text: Now let's be realistic. How many people do you need to reach for one sale? How many hours will you spend? What do you need to start?
tasks.reflection_prompt: If this acquisition plan fails, what's your backup plan? Always have a Plan B.

quests.title: The Financials

badge_config.title: Financial Master
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 4: Modeled cost structures, fixed/variable costs, and unit economics profitability.

notes.title: Use the Excel template
notes.content: We've provided an Excel template to help you work through the numbers. Use it alongside the app to do the detailed work.

notes.title: The math doesn't lie
notes.content: If the numbers don't work, the business doesn't work. Don't ignore the math.

notes.title: Be honest with yourself
notes.content: First-time founders often underestimate costs and overestimate sales. Be brutal about the numbers.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 4: The Financials. You understand your costs, your unit economics, and your profitability. The numbers tell a story—are you listening?

tasks.title: What Does It Cost?
tasks.briefing_text: Let's get real about costs. Don't guess—estimate as accurately as you can. We'll use these numbers to see if your business can make money.
tasks.reflection_prompt: Look at your costs. What surprised you? What could you reduce or eliminate?

tasks.title: Understand Your Costs
tasks.briefing_text: Now let's look at your costs differently. Fixed vs variable. What happens when you sell more?
tasks.reflection_prompt: If you had to cut your costs in half, how would you do it? Would the customer experience suffer?

tasks.title: Does the Math Work?
tasks.briefing_text: The moment of truth. Does your business make money? Let's run the numbers.
tasks.reflection_prompt: If you're not making a profit, what would need to change? More sales? Higher price? Lower costs? Be specific.

quests.title: Go or No-Go

badge_config.title: Commercial Decision Maker
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 5: Evaluated unit economics objectively and made a conscious commercial call.

notes.title: The numbers don't lie
notes.content: This is the moment of truth. If the numbers don't work, the business doesn't work. Be honest with yourself.

notes.title: Iteration is okay
notes.content: If the numbers don't quite work, you can iterate. Change the price, change the MSP, change the channel. Just be specific about what you'll change.

notes.title: No-Go is a win too
notes.content: Saying 'no' to a bad business is a win. You've saved yourself time, money, and stress. Take what you've learned to the next opportunity.

quests.success_message: You've completed Mission 4: The Business Engine. You've made a conscious decision based on real numbers. This is what building a real business looks like.

tasks.title: Make the Call
tasks.briefing_text: You've done the work. You have the numbers. Now make a decision. No overthinking. Just pick.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What did you learn from this financial exercise? If you're saying 'no' to this business, what did you learn that you'll take to the next one?

ai_config.persona_prompt: You are a pragmatic business coach who helps founders make decisions based on numbers. You're direct, honest, and focused on what the data says. You don't sugarcoat—you tell founders what they need to hear, not what they want to hear.

mission5.title: Build & Launch
mission5.success_message: You've completed Mission 5: Build & Launch. You planned your build, executed your plan, gathered testers, validated your product, and launched. You're no longer a person with an idea—you're a founder with a live business. Welcome to the other side. 🎉

badge_config.title: Live Founder
badge_config.description: Completed Mission 5: Build & Launch. Built your product, validated with real testers, and launched your business into the world.

quests.title: Plan the Build

badge_config.title: Build Strategist
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 1: Set your build timeline, mapped resource requirements, and created a structured build checklist.

notes.title: Plan, but don't overplan
notes.content: A good plan gives you direction. A perfect plan keeps you from starting. Get it good enough and start building.

notes.title: Start with the end in mind
notes.content: What does 'done' look like? Work backwards from launch.

notes.title: Resources are real
notes.content: Your time, money, and tools are limited. Plan accordingly.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 1: Plan the Build. You have a timeline, a resource plan, and a build checklist. Now it's time to execute.

tasks.title: Plan Your Timeline
tasks.briefing_text: Let's set your build timeline. We'll generate suggested dates based on your project type, and you can adjust them. Remember: this is your roadmap, not a prison.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the most ambitious but realistic date you could launch? What would make that possible?

challenges.title: The 30-Day Sprint
challenges.description: Can you build and launch in 30 days? If not, what's the smallest version you can build in that time?

tasks.title: What Do You Need?
tasks.briefing_text: Let's get real about what you need to build. What do you already have? What do you need to buy? What's your budget?
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the one resource you're missing that would make this 10x easier? Can you get it?

tasks.title: Build Your Checklist
tasks.briefing_text: Now let's break down the build into actionable tasks. We'll auto-generate tasks from your features and milestones, and you can add your own.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the first thing you'll build? Start there.

quests.title: Build Dashboard

badge_config.title: Product Executioner
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 2: Executed daily build logs, managed costs, and created a working Proof of Concept.

notes.title: Build every day
notes.content: Even 15 minutes a day keeps the momentum going. Show up every day.

notes.title: Stay focused
notes.content: Don't add features. Don't change direction. Build the MSP and nothing else.

notes.title: Share your progress
notes.content: Post build logs on social media. The more people watching, the more accountable you'll be.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 2: The Build. You've built your product, tracked your costs, and have something testers can test. The foundation is solid.

tasks.title: Build Dashboard
tasks.briefing_text:
Welcome to your Build Dashboard. This is where you'll manage everything—tasks, progress, costs, and milestones. Use this until you have something testers can test. Come back to the program when your POC is ready.

Dashboard Features:
• Overview: Project status, progress, days until launch
• Task Board: Simple Kanban (To Do, In Progress, Done, Blocked)
• Progress: Timeline with milestones, days ahead/behind
• Costs: Budget vs actual, breakdown by category
• POC Check: Feature completion, cost check, viability
• Build Log: Share progress, export summary, take notes
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the one thing you're most excited to build? What's the one thing you're most nervous about?

challenges.title: The Daily Build Challenge
challenges.description: Build something every day for 7 days. Even if it's just 15 minutes. Report your progress.

quests.title: Get Testers

badge_config.title: Tester Recruiter
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 3: Recruited target users, onboarded testers, and collected actionable product feedback.

notes.title: Testers are gold
notes.content: Real feedback from real users is the most valuable thing you can get. Don't waste it.

notes.title: Listen to understand, not to defend
notes.content: When testers give feedback, don't defend your product. Just listen.

notes.title: Start with your squad
notes.content: Your cheer squad from Mission 1 is the perfect place to start. They already want you to succeed.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 3: Get Testers. You've recruited, onboarded, and collected feedback from testers. You have real data to work with.

tasks.title: Find Your Testers
tasks.briefing_text: Who will test your product? You need real people who have the problem you're solving. Start with your squad, then expand.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the best place to find people who have this problem? That's where your testers are.

challenges.title: The 5-Tester Challenge
challenges.description: Get 5 people to test your product. Not friends and family—real potential customers.

tasks.title: Onboard Your Testers
tasks.briefing_text: How will you onboard testers? What instructions will you give them? How will they know what to do?
tasks.reflection_prompt: Put yourself in your tester's shoes. What would you need to know to give helpful feedback?

tasks.title: Collect Feedback
tasks.briefing_text: What did your testers say? What did you learn? What surprised you? What are you going to change?
tasks.reflection_prompt: What was the most surprising piece of feedback? What will you do with it?

quests.title: Validate & Tweak

badge_config.title: Product Optimizer
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 4: Performed validation checks and executed essential pre-launch tweaks.

notes.title: Validation is not perfection
notes.content: You're not looking for perfection. You're looking for 'good enough to launch.'

notes.title: Listen to the patterns
notes.content: If one tester says something, it's an opinion. If three testers say it, it's a pattern. Act on patterns.

notes.title: Don't over-iterate
notes.content: You can always improve after launch. Don't let perfect be the enemy of launched.

quests.success_message: You've completed Quest 4: Validate & Tweak. You've validated your product with real users and made meaningful improvements. You're ready to launch.

tasks.title: Validation Check
tasks.briefing_text: Based on tester feedback, is your product ready? Do people want this? Would they pay for it? Let's check.
tasks.reflection_prompt: If you had to launch today, would you? Why or why not?

tasks.title: Final Tweaks Plan
tasks.briefing_text: What changes are you making before launch? Be specific. What will you change, and how long will it take?
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the smallest change that would make the biggest difference?

quests.title: Launch

badge_config.title: Launch Pioneer
badge_config.description: Completed Quest 5: Completed the launch checklist, made the final launch call, and went live.

notes.title: Launch is not the end
notes.content: Launch is the beginning. Your real work starts when people start buying.

notes.title: Perfect is the enemy of launched
notes.content: If you're waiting for perfect, you'll never launch. Good enough is good enough.

notes.title: Celebrate this moment
notes.content: You're about to do what most people never do: launch a real business. Be proud.

quests.success_message: You've completed Mission 5: Build & Launch. You've launched your business. You're no longer a person with an idea—you're a founder with a live business. Welcome to the other side. 🎉

tasks.title: Launch Checklist
tasks.briefing_text: Before you launch, let's run through the checklist. Is everything ready?
tasks.reflection_prompt: If you had to launch right now, what would you be worried about?

challenges.title: The First Sale Challenge
challenges.description: Launch and get your first real customer. Not a friend, not family—a real customer.

tasks.title: Launch Decision
tasks.briefing_text: It's time. Is your product ready to launch? Make the call.
tasks.reflection_prompt: What's the scariest part of launching? What excites you the most?

ai_config.persona_prompt: You are a pragmatic launch coach who helps founders make the final decision to launch. You focus on readiness signals, not fear. You help founders recognize that 'good enough' is the right time to launch. You remind them that launch is the beginning, not the end.
